summary.overall: Hunting Matthew Nichols drops viewers into a chilling mockumentary: 23 years after her brother vanished on Vancouver Island, Tara Nichols (Miranda MacDougall) launches a found footage investigation. Director Markian Tarasiuk plays himself, blurring docu-reality with horror as unearthed 2001 VHS footage reveals two teens lost in haunted woods. The film satirizes true crime obsession while delivering Blair Witch-style dread: shaky cams, forest isolation, ambiguous supernatural hints. Runtime clocks 89 minutes of escalating unease, no jump-scare spam, just creeping inevitability. Festival buzz earned Tarasiuk Best Found Footage at FilmQuest and Best Director at Blood in the Snow. Pre-release, it promises authentic indie horror for fans tired of franchise slogs.
summary.adultInsight: This debut nails found footage's primal power: man's hubris against nature's unknown. Tarasiuk's meta-layer mocks Netflix true crime binges, critiquing spectacle over substance without preaching. Pure genre thrill.
summary.parentalGuidance: Not rated yet, expect R/14A. Supernatural horror, disappearance trauma, implied violence. Teens 16+ ok with psychological tension.
